title: PAY BACK, AND ADD A FIFTH

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'They must make restitution for what they have failed to do in regard to the holy things, pay an additional penalty of a fifth of the value and give it all to the priest. The priest will make atonement for them with the ram as a guilt offering, and they will be forgiven.'" - Lev 5:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Restitution, plus twenty per cent.

This is where Leviticus gets uncomfortably practical. Confession was required, and a sacrifice was required — but so was payment. God did not let the worshipper feel forgiven while the person he had wronged remained out of pocket.

Real repentance costs something.

Zacchaeus understood this instinctively. When Christ came into his life, he did not merely weep — he said, "Here and now I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have cheated anybody out of anything, I will pay back four times the amount" (Lk 19:8). Jesus' response was immediate: today salvation has come to this house.

We must be careful here. Restitution does not purchase forgiveness — verse 16 makes clear that atonement came through the ram, not through the payment. But genuine repentance produces action. Paul told Agrippa that he preached repentance and turning to God, demonstrated by their deeds (Acts 26:20).

Is there a debt you have quietly let slide? Money owed, credit taken that belonged to someone else, a reputation you damaged and never repaired?

Grace forgives freely. It also gets you moving.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there anyone I have wronged whom I have never actually made things right with?
2. Do my repentances produce action, or only feeling?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your forgiveness is free. Give me the courage to make right what I have damaged, not to earn Your mercy but because I have received it. Amen.
